<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                     </jats:title><jats:p>We classify the critical points of the effective black hole potential which governs the attractor mechanism taking place at the horizon of static dyonic extremal black holes in <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 2, <jats:italic>D</jats:italic> = 4 Maxwell-Einstein supergravity with U(1) Fayet-Iliopoulos gaugings. We use a manifestly symplectic covariant formalism, and we consider both spherical and hyperbolic horizons, recognizing the relevant sub-classes to which some representative examples belong. We also exploit projective special Kähler geometry of vector multiplets scalar manifolds, the <jats:italic>U</jats:italic>-duality-invariant quartic structure (and 2-polarizations thereof) in order to retrieve and generalize various expressions of the entropy of asymptotically AdS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> BPS black holes, in the cases in which the scalar manifolds are symmetric spaces. Finally, we present a novel static extremal black hole solution to the <jats:italic>STU</jats:italic> model, in which the dilaton interpolates between an hyperbolic near-horizon geometry and AdS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> at infinity.</jats:p>
title: Black hole attractors and U(1) Fayet-Iliopoulos gaugings: analysis and classification
